root_cause.text: ib_uverbs_post_send() in the RDMA uverbs subsystem trusted the user-controlled cmd.wqe_size to size a kmalloc buffer for struct ib_uverbs_send_wr without verifying it was at least the structure size, causing subsequent field accesses to read past the allocated heap object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (cmd.wqe_size < sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr)) return -EINVAL;` immediately before `kmalloc(cmd.wqe_size, ...)`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly says `cmd.wqe_size` was used “without any validation” so small values let accesses to `user_wr->opcode`, `user_wr->num_sge`, and other fields go out of bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation for undersized send work request buffers and suppress allocation warnings in the ib_uverbs post-send path.
intent_record.what: The code adds a check that returns -EINVAL when cmd.wqe_size is smaller than sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr), and it changes the subsequent kmalloc call to use GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_NOWARN instead of GFP_KERNEL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents attempting to process or allocate a work request buffer that is too small to hold the required send work request structure, causing invalid user input to fail early with -EINVAL. Adding __GFP_NOWARN also suppresses allocator warning messages for this allocation path when allocation fails.

grouping_result.intent: Add validation for undersized send work request buffers and suppress allocation warnings in the ib_uverbs post-send path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly validates undersized send work request buffers in ib_uverbs_post_send(), addressing the root cause that user-controlled cmd.wqe_size could be smaller than struct ib_uverbs_send_wr and lead to out-of-bounds reads after allocation.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the work request buffer using the user-controlled cmd.wqe_size without validating that it is at least large enough for struct ib_uverbs_send_wr, enabling later field accesses to read past the end of the allocated heap object.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates the send work request buffer based solely on the user-controlled cmd.wqe_size without verifying it is at least sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr). Subsequent accesses to fields of struct ib_uverbs_send_wr can therefore read past the end of the allocated heap object when cmd.wqe_size is too small.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function `ib_uverbs_post_send()` is fully shown, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause is trusting user-controlled `cmd.wqe_size` for `kmalloc()` without ensuring it is at least `sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr)`, followed by accesses through `user_wr`. In this snippet, the function explicitly checks `if (cmd.wqe_size < sizeof (struct ib_uverbs_send_wr)) return -EINVAL;` before `user_wr = kmalloc(cmd.wqe_size, GFP_KERNEL);`. That means the allocated buffer is guaranteed to be large enough for subsequent field accesses such as `user_wr->num_sge`, `user_wr->wr_id`, `user_wr->opcode`, `user_wr->send_flags`, `user_wr->imm_data`, and nested union members like `user_wr->wr.ud.ah` or `user_wr->wr.rdma.remote_addr`. Because the size validation is present before allocation and dereference, the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is already present.
